solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Furniture component well attached to lower surface (9)

indicators.note: puts the well after the lower surface, joining the two pieces

blocks.note: a bed is the lowest surface, as in a sea bed or river bed
a spring is a natural well, where water rises

annotation.surface: A description from a furniture catalogue of a part fixed to the underside of something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like an adverb, as in 'well attached', and it is the noun: a source of water. 'Lower surface' reads as the underside of the furniture, and it is a bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A bedspring is one of the coiled springs inside a bed or mattress, a component of a piece of furniture.

entries.clue: Inferior shelters engineers exposed (5)

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it inside, so BAD takes RE in

blocks.note: inferior = bad, poor in quality
RE = Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

annotation.surface: Poor-quality shelters built by army engineers are left open to the elements.
annotation.walkthrough: RE for the Royal Engineers is a standard crossword abbreviation. BAD opens around it: BA + RE + D.
annotation.definitionFit: Bared means uncovered, laid open to view, which is exposed.

entries.clue: Not totally evident a lass is tantalising healthcare worker (6,9)

indicators.note: the answer is not all of the words, just a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run starts after EVI in 'evident' and stops before ALISING in 'tantalising'

annotation.surface: Someone half-noticing a flirtatious young woman who happens to work in a clinic.
annotation.walkthrough: A fifteen-letter hidden answer is rare, which is why it hides so well; the run starts inside 'evident' and stops inside 'tantalising'.
annotation.definitionFit: A dental assistant works alongside a dentist, so is a healthcare worker.

entries.clue: Splendid taking up tour of chambers overlooking river (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up turns it to read bottom to top
to overlook something is to leave it out, so R drops from ATRIAL

blocks.note: a lap is a tour of a circuit; taken up, it reads PAL
ATRIAL (of atria, chambers of the heart) with R for river left out

annotation.surface: Someone admiring a guided tour of grand rooms that look out over a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Overlooking river' paints a view from a window, and it means ignoring the R. 'Of chambers' is the adjective ATRIAL, since atria are heart chambers.
annotation.definitionFit: Palatial means like a palace, splendid and grand.

entries.clue: Where circus acts perform bounds of lunacy with determination (8)

indicators.note: the bounds of a word are its edges, its first and last letters

blocks.note: circus acts perform in a tent, the big top
the first and last letters of LunacY

annotation.surface: A description of circus performers going at their mad stunts with total commitment.
annotation.walkthrough: The circus clause is a cryptic description that gives two words, IN TENT, run together.
annotation.definitionFit: To do something intently is to do it with fixed purpose and determination.

entries.clue: Happen to stop working (2,4)

blocks.note: slang: 'what's going down?' means what is happening
a computer system goes down when it fails

annotation.surface: An instruction or a worry that a machine might just pack up by chance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Happen to' reads as one phrase, 'chance to', and the split falls after 'Happen'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: events go down, and servers go down.

entries.clue: Revolutionary way figure presents (5)

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the pieces read backwards

blocks.note: St = street, a way
fig. = figure, as in a textbook caption

annotation.surface: A radical new way of presenting numbers or a diagram.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Presents' sits at the end looking like a verb, as if a figure were presenting something, and it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: presents here is the noun, things given, not the verb.

entries.clue: Turning fat, short skinny monkey (6)

definitions.note: a gibbon is strictly an ape, not a monkey; the clue uses the loose everyday sense

indicators.note: turning a word round makes it read backwards
a short word is missing its last letter

blocks.note: BIG (fat) turned round
BONY (skinny) cut short, losing its Y

annotation.surface: A monkey that was plump becoming thin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fat' and 'skinny' look like a contradiction the surface is describing; each is simply a piece of wordplay, one reversed and one shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: The gibbon is a long-armed tree-swinging primate, loosely called a monkey.

entries.clue: Breaking down feelings with Capitol riots (7,2,6)

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Someone emotionally overwhelmed by news of the riot at the US Capitol.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two fodder words, and 'riots' at the end stirs all fifteen letters. The Capitol is the US Congress building in Washington.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone falling to pieces is breaking down, losing control.

entries.clue: Tattered rag’s first of many torn using physical force (6-3)

indicators.note: something tattered is torn to shreds, so the letters are rearranged
takes only the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the first letter of Many
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An old rag, ripped apart by many hands, is torn by brute force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Torn' looks like a second anagram indicator, echoing 'Tattered', and it is fodder: its letters go into the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: Strong-arm describes tactics that rely on force or threats.

entries.clue: Call telephone number about lock (7)

indicators.note: turns the telephone abbreviation about, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: to ring someone is to call them
TEL., the abbreviation seen before a telephone number, turned about

annotation.surface: Phoning a locksmith about a door lock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lock' is not the door kind but a lock of hair. TEL. is the abbreviation printed in front of a phone number.
annotation.definitionFit: Lock is taken in its hair sense, and the answer names one curled strand of that kind.

entries.clue: Amateur mural ultimately delineated with felt-tip pen (7)

indicators.note: takes the ultimate, or last, letter
to delineate is to outline, so the pen draws round the L

blocks.note: a dabber is a felt-tip marker, as used to mark bingo cards
the last letter of muraL

annotation.surface: A hobbyist painting a mural and finishing its outline with a marker pen.
annotation.walkthrough: The L sits in the middle of the pen. A dabber, or dauber, is the chunky felt-tip used to mark numbers at bingo, a British sense many solvers will not know.
annotation.definitionFit: A dabbler takes up something casually, without professional commitment: an amateur.

entries.clue: Discussed current plan (5)

indicators.note: what is discussed is spoken, so the word is said rather than spelt

blocks.note: a draught is a current of air

annotation.surface: A meeting talking over the plan now in force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as an adjective, present, and it is a noun: a draught of air. DRAUGHT is the British spelling; DRAFT sounds the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a rough first version of a scheme or document is also its plan.

entries.clue: Scientist’s novel shocked nation (9)

indicators.note: shocked hair stands every which way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: novel = new
NATION rearranged

annotation.surface: A scientist writes a novel that scandalises the whole country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, and it is the adjective NEW. The definition is the possessive 'Scientist’s', meaning belonging to Newton, the scientist.
annotation.definitionFit: Newtonian means of or belonging to Isaac Newton, the scientist.

entries.clue: Scraps publicity charges for boring items (8)

indicators.note: to charge something is to load it, so BRAWLS is filled with AD

blocks.note: scraps = fights, brawls
an ad is publicity

annotation.surface: A company cutting its advertising fees for dull products.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' looks like a verb, discards, and it is the noun: fights. 'Boring' reads as dull, and it means drilling holes.
annotation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small pointed tool for boring holes in wood.

entries.clue: Discuss speed on a cycle (3,6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so BAT comes first

blocks.note: bat = speed, as in 'going at a fair bat'
as written
a round is a cycle, as of events or duties

annotation.surface: Talking things over while riding fast on a bicycle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' looks like a bicycle, and it is a round. 'At a great bat' is British slang for at high speed.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: tossing an idea back and forth like a ball is a way to discuss it.

entries.clue: Asian city a German visited regularly (4)

indicators.note: calling at letters at regular intervals picks out every other one

blocks.note: as written
the odd letters of GeRmAn

annotation.surface: A German tourist who keeps going back to an Asian city.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface says the German visited the city; in the wordplay the German is the word visited, letter by letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Agra is the city in India that is home to the Taj Mahal.

entries.clue: Dispirited and fed up with tardy daughter (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: FED written upwards
tardy = late
d = daughter, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A parent sick of a daughter who is always late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' reads as the idiom, sick of, and it splits: FED with 'up' as the instruction to reverse it.
annotation.definitionFit: Deflated means having lost confidence or spirit.

entries.clue: Thoroughly investigates lodgings of Parisian with record (4,4)

blocks.note: digs is British slang for rented lodgings
de is French for 'of'
an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: A detective looking into a Parisian's rented rooms and his criminal record.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of Parisian' means the word for 'of' in French, DE, not something belonging to a Parisian.
annotation.definitionFit: To dig deep is to investigate thoroughly, going beyond the surface.

entries.clue: Shy to caress, releasing anxiety (4)

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go, so CARE leaves CARESS

blocks.note: as written
CARESS letting go of CARE (anxiety)

annotation.surface: A timid person reluctant to be touched, until the nerves melt away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like the adjective, timid, and it is the verb: to throw, as at a coconut shy.
annotation.definitionFit: Shy is the verb meaning to throw, the sense kept in 'coconut shy', a fairground stall.

entries.clue: Live in backward sleepy area somewhere in Spain (8)

indicators.note: reads the word the wrong way round

blocks.note: to be is to live, exist
IN reversed
a dorm (dormitory) is where people sleep

annotation.surface: Settling down in a sleepy, behind-the-times corner of Spain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backward' reads as describing a sleepy rural backwater, and it only turns IN round. Benidorm is a busy Spanish seaside resort, anything but sleepy.
annotation.definitionFit: Benidorm is a resort town on Spain's Costa Blanca.

entries.clue: Cross top of range by climbing concealed nets (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter
in a down clue, climbing means read upwards
to net something is to catch it inside, so HID holds the reversed letters

blocks.note: concealed = hid
R (top of Range) + BY, written upwards

annotation.surface: An angry climber crossing a summit and finding hidden nets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry or a verb, and it is the noun: a crossbreed.
annotation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of a cross between two species or varieties.

entries.clue: Look chestnut horse over (6)

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the pieces read backwards

blocks.note: chestnut is a reddish-brown colour
a nag is an old horse

annotation.surface: A request to examine a chestnut horse.
annotation.walkthrough: RED + NAG turned over gives GANDER. 'Chestnut' is a horse's coat colour, which is why the surface reads so naturally. 'Take a gander' is British slang for have a look.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: 'take a gander' means have a look, so the noun stands for a glance.

entries.clue: Lacking practice, fix cocktail (5,4)

blocks.note: a skill gets rusty without practice
to nail something is to fix it in place

annotation.surface: Someone out of practice trying to make a mixed drink.
annotation.walkthrough: A rusty nail is a cocktail of Scotch whisky and Drambuie.
annotation.definitionFit: The rusty nail is a well-known whisky cocktail.

entries.clue: Sketch encapsulates back of designer garment (5)

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose, so SKIT holds the R
the back of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a skit is a short comic sketch
the last letter of designeR

annotation.surface: A fashion drawing that shows the back view of a designer outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sketch' belongs with the designer in the surface, as a fashion drawing, and it is a comic skit.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one kind of garment, worn from the waist down.

entries.clue: River split after type of junction (5)

indicators.note: 'after' in an across or down clue means placed later in reading order, so RENT follows T

blocks.note: a T-junction, where one road meets another at right angles
a rent is a split or tear

annotation.surface: A river dividing where the roads meet.
annotation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
annotation.definitionFit: The Trent is one of England's longest rivers.

entries.clue: Following cut, Freudian slips not broadcast (7)

indicators.note: F, following, is cut from the word
a slip is a mistake, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: FREUDIAN with F (following) cut

annotation.surface: After a scandal, a presenter's Freudian slips never make it on air.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Freudian slips' is one phrase in the surface; here 'slips' is the anagram signal. F for following is a standard abbreviation, as in 'p. 3 f.'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a programme never put on air has not been broadcast.

entries.clue: Foodstuff from plant covering lake roughly to the west (7)

indicators.note: TREE covers, or goes round, the other letters
in an across clue west is leftward, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: a tree is a plant
L (lake) + CA (circa, roughly) written leftwards

annotation.surface: A food produced by a plant growing round a lake, somewhere westward.
annotation.walkthrough: CA, short for circa, means roughly. Treacle is the British name for molasses or golden syrup.
annotation.definitionFit: Treacle is a syrup from sugar refining, a foodstuff.

entries.clue: Old obsolete Tesla parts returned (5)

indicators.note: T parts DEAD, splitting it in two
the result is sent back, reading right to left

blocks.note: obsolete = dead, no longer in use
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

annotation.surface: An old Tesla car, its outdated parts sent back to the maker.
annotation.walkthrough: DE + T + AD makes DETAD, which reads DATED backwards. 'Parts' looks like car components, and it is a verb: T parts DEAD.
annotation.definitionFit: Dated means old-fashioned, belonging to an earlier time.

entries.clue: Set period to tidy up place again (9)

indicators.note: to tidy up is to rearrange, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A fixed time slot allotted for tidying a place up again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set period' reads as a fixed time, and its nine letters are the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To redeposit something is to place or lay it down again.
